rationale: Round 0 compiled and ran correctly with no ICE, so the headroom exists to push obfuscation intensity up across the board. This is a tiny C++ program (14 functions, ~3.3KB text) whose reverse-engineering value is concentrated in main and the Garage constructors/listVehicles, so control-flow-centric passes get the highest security weights: BCF and FLA lead (0.85/0.8) to flatten and bog down the main dispatch logic, with SUB (0.8) applied aggressively since arithmetic substitution is cheap and safe in this small integer-heavy workload. SPLIT is weighted mainly for diversity (0.7) because it composes well with FLA at near-zero runtime cost and enlarges the surface FLA transforms. IBR stays fairly high (0.75) to insert opaque branching, while ICALL and IGV are kept moderately high but with elevated correctness-risk weights (0.25/0.2) since indirect-call and global-variable transformations are the likeliest sources of subtle breakage in C++ code with constructors and global init (_GLOBAL__sub_I). Cost weights are raised from a conservative baseline but capped below the security weights so the selector still favors applying passes, accepting the modest runtime/size growth a 128-line benchmark can afford.
